markets.rules_primary: If the value of the S&P 500 index, as calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, on December 1, 2026 at 10:14:59 AM EST is at least 6800.00, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 1, 2026 at 10:15am EST: the S&P 500 value as of 10:14:59 AM EST on December 1, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. The named economic event provides context; a delayed or rescheduled release does not automatically move the observation time.

Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the S&P Dow Jones Indices. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the election results are certified.
markets.rules_primary: If Josh Turek's margin of victory outperforms that of the Real Clear Polling average at 10 AM ET on Nov 3, 2026 in the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Iowa, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The market compares the official certified election result to the specified poll or polling average. "Outperform" means the actual result exceeds the poll figure; "underperform" means it falls short. Only certified results count - not preliminary tallies or projections. If using a poll range, the midpoint is used for comparison. Margins of error are not considered; any difference counts as over/underperformance.

For the purposes of this market, the Real Clear Polling average for the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Iowa at 10 AM ET on November 3, 2026 is used to determine relative performance. At that time the average was Turek 47.1%, Hinson 47.1% (tied), so Josh Turek's polling margin is 0.0 points. Josh Turek outperforms only by winning outright: the certified margin of victory must be greater than 0.0 points, and a tie does not count.

For a winning candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate's vote share and their closest competitor's share. For a losing candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate’s vote share and the vote share of the candidate immediately ahead of them. Positive margins indicate the candidate won, negative margins indicate they lost, and zero indicates a tie. The polling margin is calculated the same way from the RCP Average figures, so a deficit in the average is a negative margin. Vote shares are percentages of all votes cast for the office.

Write-in votes are aggregated as a single candidate if not individually reported. Only certified results are used for resolution. Certification by the competent authority is the final result, even if later challenged, recounted, or litigated.
markets.title: Will Josh Turek outperform the Real Clear Polling average in the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Iowa?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the visit occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If Donald Trump has physically travelled to and been present within the geographic boundaries of Alaska on or after Nov 1, 2026 and before Dec 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The following do NOT constitute a visit:

Flying over the area without landing
Layovers during which the person remains in an airplane
Virtual or remote appearances
Presence in international waters adjacent to the area
Presence solely within embassy or consulate grounds
Plans, announcements, or scheduling of future visits that do not occur during the applicable time period

For the avoidance of doubt, a visit occurs only when the person exits an aircraft, vehicle, vessel, or train within the area, or otherwise physically enters the area not aboard one. Remaining aboard, including during flyovers, drive-throughs, and non-exit refueling stops, does not constitute a visit. Exiting within the area constitutes a visit regardless of duration or method of exit.

markets.rules_primary: If CISA adds at least 10 vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog with a Date Added from Nov 1, 2026 through Nov 30, 2026 (as checked at cisa.gov at 10:00 AM ET on Dec 1, 2026), then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved

The market solely resolves to the dates visibly displayed as "Date Added" in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog at 10:00 AM ET on Dec 1, 2026.
The month runs from Nov 1, 2026 through Nov 30, 2026.

Payout criteria

Each CVE entry with a Date Added within that period counts once.
Entries are counted by their displayed Date Added, not by the date CISA announces them.

custom_strike.Person: an equipment, software, power or telecommunications failure

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If a Source Agency confirms after Issuance and before Dec 1, 2026 that an equipment, software, power or telecommunications failure caused the FAA's nationwide ground stop on Nov 13, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This must be confirmed, verified, or established as factual by at least one Source Agency.

The ground stop is the nationwide departure ground stop the FAA ordered on Nov 13, 2026. A cause counts if a Source Agency reports it as a cause of the ground stop or of the radio, radar or other system outage behind it. More than one market can resolve to Yes.

System failure: a malfunction of hardware, software, power or telecommunications equipment used by the FAA or its contractors, including one set off by maintenance work or accidental damage. A cyberattack, jamming or sabotage is not a failure.
Maintenance/upgrade: planned maintenance, an upgrade, a configuration change or a cutover on an FAA or contractor system
Physical damage: accidental damage to a cable, line, antenna or other physical equipment, including by construction work or weather
Software/config error: a fault in software, or a wrong setting or configuration, in an FAA or contractor system, including one introduced by an update or upgrade
Contractor failure: the failure, damage, error or work behind the outage was in equipment, a network or a system run by a company other than the FAA, such as a telecommunications carrier or an FAA contractor
SMART system: a malfunction or error in, or the deployment or rollout of, the FAA's SMART air traffic management system, including its interaction with other FAA systems
Human error: a mistake by a person, such as an FAA employee, air traffic controller, technician or contractor, set off the outage, including a wrong command, setting, procedure or physical action. A deliberate act meant to disrupt equipment or operations does not count.
AI system error: an AI system or AI agent (a machine-learning model, large language model or autonomous agent) itself produced the action, output or change that caused the outage, and the Source Agency describes that system as AI. It does not count if AI was only part of the affected system, used by staff or contractors, running at the time, or used to help write software that later failed.
Specific cause confirmed: a Source Agency confirms what caused the telecommunications outage behind the ground stop by naming a particular malfunction, error, damage or other event. If no cause is confirmed before Dec 1, 2026, this market resolves to No.
L3Harris: the failure, damage, error or work behind the outage was in equipment, a network or a system that L3Harris Technologies runs, manages or oversees for the FAA, whoever caused it
Verizon: the failure, damage, error or work behind the outage was in equipment, a network or a system that Verizon runs, manages or oversees for the FAA, whoever caused it

The following do NOT count:
A report that a cause is suspected, being investigated or has not been ruled out
A statement that the ground stop followed a communication, radio or radar outage or issue, without saying what caused that outage
A cause of a different outage or ground stop

This market is NOT mutually exclusive: more than one market can resolve to Yes. For example, a problem with the SMART rollout can also count for Maintenance/upgrade and, if it is a software or configuration fault, for Software/config error.

Maintenance/upgrade: planned maintenance, an upgrade, a configuration change or a cutover on an FAA or contractor system
Physical damage: accidental damage to a cable, line, antenna or other physical equipment, including by construction work or weather
Software/config error: a fault in software, or a wrong setting or configuration, in an FAA or contractor system, including one introduced by an update or upgrade
Contractor failure: the failure, damage, error or work behind the outage was in equipment, a network or a system run by a company other than the FAA, such as a telecommunications carrier or an FAA contractor
SMART system: a malfunction or error in, or the deployment or rollout of, the FAA's SMART air traffic management system, including its interaction with other FAA systems
Human error: a mistake by a person, such as an FAA employee, air traffic controller, technician or contractor, set off the outage, including a wrong command, setting, procedure or physical action. A deliberate act meant to disrupt equipment or operations does not count.
AI system error: an AI system or AI agent (a machine-learning model, large language model or autonomous agent) itself produced the action, output or change that caused the outage, and the Source Agency describes that system as AI. It does not count if AI was only part of the affected system, used by staff or contractors, running at the time, or used to help write software that later failed.
Specific cause confirmed: a Source Agency confirms what caused the telecommunications outage behind the ground stop by naming a particular malfunction, error, damage or other event. If no cause is confirmed before Dec 1, 2026, this market resolves to No.
L3Harris: the failure, damage, error or work behind the outage was in equipment, a network or a system that L3Harris Technologies runs, manages or oversees for the FAA, whoever caused it
Verizon: the failure, damage, error or work behind the outage was in equipment, a network or a system that Verizon runs, manages or oversees for the FAA, whoever caused it

The following do NOT count:
A report that a cause is suspected, being investigated or has not been ruled out
A statement that the ground stop followed a communication, radio or radar outage or issue, without saying what caused that outage
A cause of a different outage or ground stop

This market is NOT mutually exclusive: more than one market can resolve to Yes. For example, a problem with the SMART rollout can also count for Maintenance/upgrade and, if it is a software or configuration fault, for Software/config error.

Period: November 1, 2026 at 12:00 AM EDT to December 1, 2026 at 12:00 AM EST. Includes the start; excludes the end.
Source: PJM Data Miner 2’s verified hourly real-time total LMPs. Intervals follow their Eastern-time start times; repeated daylight-saving hours count separately.
Calculation: Simple average of all applicable hourly prices, including negative prices. Round the average to two decimals, with exact halves away from zero. Equality resolves No.
Trading closes: November 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. The final delivery interval still counts.
Price versions: Use first published applicable prices. Later corrections count only if published before expiration and accepted by the Exchange as correcting a material error. Exclude unverified, estimated, indicative and forecast prices.
Missing data: Do not fill missing prices. At expiration, average the available prices if at least 95% of required intervals are available. Below 95%, resolve only if the available data establishes the outcome regardless of missing values; otherwise, settle at the Exchange-determined last fair price under the full rules.

When confirming the settlement value, note the close price for the 1-minute candlestick at a given time is the price at the end of the immediately preceding one-minute interval. For example, the candlestick timestamped 4:59 PM reflects trading during 4:59:00 PM to 4:59:59 PM and closes at 5:00:00 PM. If no data is published by the specified source agency for the specified time, then the most recently available published data will be used to resolve the market.
